contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned to understand what you read. This week: learn to write it! We'll build one complete paragraph, one piece at a time.

Every paragraph starts with a topic sentence — one sentence that tells the main idea of what the whole paragraph will be about. A good topic sentence is clear and specific. 'I like my dog.' is a topic sentence about a dog. 'Things exist.' is too vague to be a good topic sentence. Practice: write a topic sentence about your favorite season. Make sure it clearly names your topic (which season) and your main idea about it.
You just wrote a real topic sentence — the first building block of a paragraph! Tomorrow we'll add supporting details.

objectives: Understand that a topic sentence states a paragraph's main idea
Write a clear, specific topic sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's reading-comprehension strategies briefly.
2. Introduce the topic sentence, comparing the dog example to the too-vague example.
3. Have the child write a topic sentence about their favorite season.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's supporting-details lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a sentence starter like 'My favorite season is ___ because ___.'
Ready for more: ask the child to write two different topic sentences about the same season, each with a different main idea
This week builds one paragraph across all 5 days — keep the child's own chosen topic consistent from today onward
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended writing activity — check that the child's topic sentence is clear, specific, and names a real topic (not vague like 'Things happen.').
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 Writing standard W.2.1/W.2.2 (informative/opinion writing with a clear topic), opening this week's paragraph-writing thread from the course's own description.
